BACKGROUND
In connection with the proposed master planned development of an area known as Ritter
Ranch (“Project”), the City formed the City of Palmdale Community Facilities District 93-
1 (“CFD 93-1”) to finance certain public facilities for the Project. The City issued Special
Tax Bonds for CFD 93-1 in 1995 for that purpose (“93-1 Bonds”). The outstanding 93-1
Bonds were purchased by Preston Hollow Capital, LLC (“PHC”) in 2018. In 2020, PHC
also acquired the property within CFD 93-1 and transferred the land to RdR
Development Holdings, LLC (“RdR”), a limited liability company for which PHC is the
sole member. Collectively, PHC and RdR are referred to below as the RdR Parties. PHC
continues to own the 93-1 Bonds, and RdR continues to own the property within CFD
93-1.
In September 2022, the RdR Parties were prepared to proceed with the development of
the first phase of the Project, which is expected to include up to 1,180 residential units
(“Phase 1”). They requested, and the City formed, a new community facilities district for
the Phase 1 property portion of the Project (“CFD 2022-3”) to fund public infrastructure
and improvements necessary for the development of the Project and to refinance a
portion of the 93-1 Bonds, the removal of the Phase 1 property from CFD 93-1 and
elimination of the CFD 93-1 special tax levy on the Phase 1 property. The RdR Parties
have since decided to cancel all the outstanding CFD 93-1 Bonds before proceeding
with the issuance of special tax bonds for CFD 2022-3.
It has been determined that, at this time, additional actions are needed for CFD 93-1 to
accomplish the termination of the special tax lien relating to outstanding 93-1 Bonds
upon cancellation of the 93-1 Bonds.

DISCUSSION
During the CFD 2022-3 formation process, the Phase 1 property was removed from
CFD 93-1 and is now included in CFD 2022-3. At that time, the lien of 93-1 Bonds on
the new CFD 2022-3 property was extinguished. Subsequently, it was determined that
removing the Phase 1 property from CFD 93-1 was premature and affected the ability
to terminate the special tax lien relating to the 93-1 Bonds when they are canceled.
To remedy this, certain administrative actions are necessary. First, the Phase 1 property
must be annexed back into CFD 93-1. Second, the Rate and Method of Apportionment
of Special Taxes (“RMA”) for CFD 93-1 must be amended to provide that once the 93-1
Bonds are canceled, the lien of CFD 93-1 Bonds and related special taxes on the
property within CFD 93-1, including the Phase 1 property will then be terminated.
The process to annex the Phase 1 property into CFD 93-1 starts with RdR filing a petition
with the City requesting that the City Council undertake the annexation proceedings.
The petition includes a request that the City hold a special election authorizing the City
to (a) annex property to CFD 93-1 and (b) alter the RMA for CFD 93-1. RdR has filed

the petition with the City. PHC, as the sole owner of the 93-1 Bonds, has also filed a
consent to the alteration of the RMA for CFD 93-1.
With the petition and the consent received, the City Council can consider adopting a
resolution declaring its intention to annex the Phase 1 property into CFD 93-1. The City
Council can then consider adopting a resolution of consideration to amend the RMA for
CFD 93-1 to provide for the termination of the CFD 93-1 lien on the Phase 1 Property
once the 93-1 Bonds are canceled later this year.

Future Actions
Each resolution sets a time and place for the separate public hearings on the annexation
of property into CFD 93-1 and the alteration of the RMA for CFD 93-1, both of which are
proposed to be November 15, 2023, at 5:00 pm.

(AVAQMD) in the amount of $233,506 and approve an agreement with Electrical Vehicle
Charging Stations (EVCS) for the purchase and installation of charging stations for
$233,506.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Accept a $233,506 grant provided by AVAQMD through Agreement No. A-8481
  and appropriate the funds for twelve (12) Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Stations
  at McAdam Park; and,
  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8485 in
  the amount of $233,506 with EVCS for the purchase and installation of twelve (12)
  EV Charging Stations, including non-substantive changes;

BACKGROUND
On May 4, 2021, the City accepted grant funds from Southern California Edison’s Self-
Generation Incentive Program for the installation of solar shade structures and a battery
storage component at McAdam Park. The City has been moving forward with the design
and installation of the batteries and added a solar component and system software
needed for the project. While working on the project and looking at all work slated for
the park, the City identified a need for approximately twelve (12) electric vehicle charging
units. It reached out to AVAQMD for possible financial assistance.
DISCUSSION
Upon discussions with AVAQMD, they recommended and approved a grant to the City
of Palmdale that will cover the full cost of purchase, installation, and maintenance of the
twelve (12) EV charging stations located at McAdam Park.

Staff recommends that the City Council approve an MOU between the City of Palmdale
(City) and the California High-Speed Rail Authority (CHSRA) that provides a framework

BACKGROUND
The CHSRA’s Palmdale Station and station site facilities are intended to serve as a
multimodal hub of seamless transit connectivity, incentivize first and last-mile
connections, and encourage integrated station area development. The City’s goals for the

will include residential, open space, and commercial development. Additionally, the future
High Desert Corridor project with Brightline West will provide high-speed rail service from
Las Vegas, intending to connect to the CHSRA’s Palmdale Station. The City and CHRSA
have participated in and continue to collaborate on planning activities about the Palmdale
Station, including but not limited to the Bakersfield to Palmdale Final EIR/EIS and
Palmdale Transit Area Specific Plan. They have collaborated in a series of workshops
since June 2022, supported by applicable stakeholder agencies, focused on advancing
key collaborative decisions regarding timing, multi-modal integration, and public/private
sector participation in the development and delivery of Palmdale Station.

partnerships, and an effective station area partnership structure to create an integrated

  B. Pursue and take advantage of funding opportunities;

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2023-066 extending the Director of Emergency
  Services’ Proclamation of a Local Emergency resulting from Tropical Storm
  Hilary; and
  2. Authorize the Director of Emergency Services or their designee to negotiate and

BACKGROUND
The National Weather Service issued a Tropical Storm Warning on August 18, 2023,
warning of conditions of damage and extreme peril to the safety of persons and property
within the City of Palmdale. On Sunday, August 20, 2023, conditions of disaster or
extreme threat to persons and property were present due to Tropical Storm Hilary, which
arrived in the City of Palmdale bringing high winds and gusts, intense precipitation,
debris flow, urban flooding, falling and downed trees, and adverse impacts to critical
infrastructure. The City of Palmdale received approximately six inches of rain in a 24-
hour period.
 Report to the Mayor and City Council

October 18, 2023
Page 2

Both public and private property sustained damage. The City virtually activated the
Emergency Operation Center in response to the emergency. City Staff were deployed to
clear roads, alleviate flooding, and inspect damaged dwellings. In addition, Victory
Outreach opened the City Community Emergency Resource Center, providing refuge
from the storm for residents in need. On August 20, 2023, the County of Los Angeles
and the State of California each declared an emergency, both in response to Tropical
Storm Hilary.
DISCUSSION
On August 24, 2023, the City’s Director of Emergency Services proclaimed the
existence of a local emergency within the City of Palmdale, pursuant to the California
Government Code Section 8630 and Municipal Code Section 2.28.040. The City Council
ratified the proclamation under Resolution CC 2023-055. The conditions resulting from
the Tropical Storm Hilary Incident warrant and necessitate the extension of the
proclamation of the existence of a local emergency due to the City continuing clean up
and repair of the impacts to critical infrastructure from Tropical Storm Hilary. Resolution
CC 2023-066 would authorize the Director of Emergency Services to continue to take
appropriate measures to protect public health, safety, and welfare and obtain
emergency aid from other agencies. In accordance with Municipal Code Section
2.28.040, the Director of Emergency Services is empowered to take actions including
but not limited to obtaining vital supplies, equipment, and such other properties found
lacking and needed for the protection of life and property and to bind the City for the fair
value thereof.

There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

environment.

  catastrophic disasters and emergencies.

BACKGROUND
The Board of Library Trustees is comprised of five (5) members, who are nominated and
appointed according to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 2.08.030. The Board
operates under the Education Code. Members serve a three-year term and must reside
in the City of Palmdale.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Hold a public hearing to accept public testimony and approve Agreement No. A-
  8522 with Crosstown Electrical & Data, Inc. for a lighting fixture retrofit project for
  $285,000;

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8522,

  3. Authorize a budget of transfer of $285,000 of unappropriated Prop A Local Return
  Fund Balance into a new CIP account, to be created upon Council approval of this
  item, for Pelona Vista Park and Ride Lights.

BACKGROUND
To comply with the State EV charging unit requirements, Staff researched and identified
parking lot lights that could accommodate electric vehicle (EV) charging units.
The identified lights are Omniflow lights, that accommodate EV charging units and
minimize grid energy requirements by incorporating solar and wind energy-generating
technologies.

In identifying the lights and the technologies used, it was determined that it was in the
City’s best interest to create a pilot project to test the proposed lights. The Pelona Vista
Park-n-Ride lot was identified as a potential site for this pilot project. The area currently
uses metal halide lights; therefore, the City could maximize energy savings with the
change out of the lights.
 Report to Mayor and City Council

DISCUSSION
The City will retrofit fifty (50) fixtures at the Pelona Vista Park-n-Ride. Upon researching
lighting vendors, Omniflow lights was the only vendor that could incorporate EV charging
technologies. Per Omniflow, Crosstown Electrical & Data is the contractor selected by
Omniflow to install their lights. Crosstown Electrical & Data will also provide training on
the upkeep and maintenance of the new lights.

The project will save the City over 100 MWh and avoid over nineteen (19) carbon dioxide
equivalent tons per year, which will significantly help with the City’s efforts to reduce
greenhouse gases. In addition to the proposed reduction in GHGs generated by the City
and having lights that will no longer be grid-dependent, this project will save over $9,000
in the first year of use alone. The retrofits will provide energy conservation, energy
efficiency, energy generation, and other energy-related capital improvement services.

Under California Government Code Section 4217.10 et seq., the City may contract with
Omniflow/Crosstown Electrical & Data if the above criteria have been met and the
Council’s review and approval of the proposed work has been publicly noticed.

Fund Balance into a new CIP account, for Pelona Vista Park and Ride Lights, to be
created upon Council approval of this item.

Staff recommends that the City Council:

BACKGROUND
In March 2023, Design Build Agreement No. A-8161 was awarded to Schneider Electric,
for $8,491,602 to implement energy-saving and operation cost-saving projects
throughout City facilities to benefit the community.

In March 2023, Schneider Electric completed an extensive investment grade analysis
and prepared a recommendation of projects for the City’s consideration, as outlined
below.
   Replacement of 42 HVAC units that are in operation beyond their useful life of 15
  years.
   Replacement and/or upgrade of building control solutions that monitor the heating
  and air systems. Many of these have obsolete systems where components are
